title: Crisp Battered White Fish Tacos with Red Cabbage and Lime Crema
summary: Crunchy sparkling-water-battered white fish in warm corn tortillas with tangy lime crema and crisp red cabbage.
equipment: large heavy pot (at least 5 l) or deep fryer
wire rack set over a baking tray

ingredients.item: skinless firm white fish fillets, such as cod or haddock
ingredients.note: cut into 12 fingers about 2 cm x 8 cm

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
mayonnaise (check the label: distilled vinegar only)
lime juice, plus the finely grated zest of the lime

steps.title: Prep the Components
steps.text: Before anything else, pat the fish fingers thoroughly dry with kitchen paper and sprinkle them with the 1/4 tsp salt. Whisk the mayonnaise, soured cream, lime juice and zest together in a small bowl to make the crema, then toss the shredded cabbage with the 1 tbsp lime juice separately. Drying the fish well matters, because any surface water stops the batter sticking and makes it spit in the hot oil.

steps.title: Heat the Frying Oil
steps.text: Hot oil needs room to bubble up safely, so pour it into the large pot — no more than one-third full — and heat over medium-high heat to 190°C on a deep-fry thermometer. Never leave the oil unattended, whether it's heating or actively frying. Keeping the pot only partly full is what gives the oil that margin of safety.

steps.title: Mix the Batter
steps.text: In a separate bowl, whisk the flour, cornflour, paprika and 1/2 tsp salt together. Once the oil is nearly at temperature, whisk in the cold egg and sparkling water just until smooth with a few small lumps left. Mixing the batter at the last minute keeps the sparkling water's bubbles lively, which is what makes the coating light and crisp rather than dense.

steps.title: Fry the Fish
steps.text: Dip four fish fingers in the batter, let the excess drip off, and lower them into the oil one at a time, away from you. Fry for 3-4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp and the fish reaches 63°C or is opaque and flakes easily. Lift onto the wire rack and let the oil return to 190°C before frying the next batch; checking temperature rather than colour alone is the more reliable doneness cue.

steps.title: Warm the Tortillas
steps.text: Heat a dry frying pan over medium-high heat and warm the tortillas one or two at a time, 20-30 seconds per side, until soft, pliable and lightly speckled. Stack them in a folded clean tea towel as they're done so trapped steam keeps them soft until serving.

steps.title: Assemble and Serve
steps.text: Top each warm tortilla with a piece of fried fish, a spoonful of dressed cabbage and a drizzle of lime crema, finishing with a few coriander leaves. Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side, since the batter is at its crispest straight from the fryer. Once frying is finished, let the oil cool completely before straining or discarding it, rather than handling it while still hot.

tips: Dry the fish thoroughly before dipping it in batter — any surface water stops the coating sticking and makes the oil spit.
Mix the batter just before frying so the sparkling water is still fizzy; a batter made too early turns flat and heavy.
Check the mayonnaise label and choose one made with distilled vinegar.
Serve the fish as soon as it's fried — it loses its crunch quickly once it sits.
safety: Let the oil cool completely before straining or discarding it; never move or strain hot oil.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten straight away. If needed, refrigerate leftover fish within 1 hour and use within 1 day, reheating in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven until piping hot (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
